nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ru/TiO2
nodes.procedure: Hydrothermal reaction of Ru precursor and Ti precursor to form Ru/TiO2 nanoparticles.
nodes.source_text: Ru/P-TiO2 NPs were synthesized by a two-step process comprising a hydrothermal reaction followed by a facile phosphorization.

nodes.name: Phosphorization and annealing
nodes.procedure: The Ru/TiO2 was mixed with NaH2PO2 at mass ratio of Ru-Ti precursor to NaH2PO2 of 1:20, phosphorized followed by annealing at 700°C. This resulted in phase transition from pure A-TiO2 to A+R TiO2 (A:R=1.3:1), with phosphorus incorporated into the TiO2 lattice as P5+ partially substituting Ti4+ to form Ti-O-P linkages. More oxygen vacancies were generated during the P-doping process due to the reducing gas H2 produced from the decomposition of sodium hypophosphite.

unit_operations.name: Annealing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: annealing temperatures after phosphorization (T = 600, 700, and 800°C), optimal at 700°C

nodes.source_text: Ru/P-TiO2 NPs were synthesized by a two-step process comprising a hydrothermal reaction followed by a facile phosphorization... a series of catalysts were synthesized using different annealing temperatures after phosphorization (T = 600, 700, and 800°C)... catalyst prepared with a Ru dosage of 10 mg and a mass ratio of Ru-Ti precursor to NaH2PO2 of 1:20 showed optimal catalytic activity.

nodes.name: P-TiO2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: P-TiO2 catalyst was prepared as comparison using similar phosphorization method on TiO2 support.
nodes.source_text: In order to better reveal the role of Ru in HER, P-TiO2 catalyst was also prepared as comparison (Figure S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and SEM images show highly porous nanoparticle morphology of Ru/P-TiO2 catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Representative transmission electron microscope (TEM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Figure S1 and S2, respectively) of the catalyst indicated a highly porous nanoparticle morphology...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows mixed phase of tetragonal anatase TiO2 (A-TiO2) (JCPDS No. 21-1272) and rutile TiO2 (R-TiO2) (JCPDS No. 03-1122) with A:R = 1.3:1, large half-peak width with weak intensity indicating ultra-small size and poor crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ...which was identified to be a mixed phase of tetragonal anatase TiO2 (A-TiO2) (JCPDS No. 21-1272) and rutile TiO2 (R-TiO2) (JCPDS No. 03-1122) (A:R = 1.3:1, determined by the integral area of the XRD diffraction peak) from the XRD pattern (Figure S3) that was characterized by a large half-peak width with weak intensity...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows Ru cluster diameter ranges from 2 to 5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on the high-angle annular dark field (HAADF)-STEM image (Figure S4), the diameter of Ru clusters ranges from 2 to 5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes corresponding to (101) planes of A-TiO2, (101) and (110) planes of R-TiO2; filtered image demonstrates inconsecutive lattice fringes and missing lattice sites confirming vacancy defects; amorphous regions with no visible lattice fringes observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure 1b) showed a series of lattice fringes corresponding to the (101) planes (Figure 1c) of A-TiO2, and the (101) and (110) planes of R-TiO2 (Figure 1d)... The filtered image in Figure 1e demonstrates the inconsecutive property of lattice fringes of R-TiO2 and the ambiguous or even missing of some lattice sites...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS demonstrates uniform distribution of O, P, Ti and Ru throughout the Ru/P-TiO2 nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometry (EDS) demonstrates the uniform distribution of O, P, Ti and Ru throughout the nanoparticles (Figure 1f).

properties.description: Series of elemental distribution maps with 50 nm scale bars

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows Ru content of 0.61 wt% and P content of 0.44 wt% in Ru/P-TiO2 NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru and P contents of the Ru/P-TiO2 NPs were approximately 0.61 and 0.44 wt% respectively, as indicated by inductively coupled plasma (ICP) atomic emission spectrometry.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms presence of Ru, P, O, Ti in Ru/P-TiO2; Ru 3d5/2 shows Ru0 negative shift (-0.06 eV vs Ru/TiO2); Ti 2p positive shift in Ru/P-TiO2; P 2p peaks at 133.2 eV and 134.3 eV indicate P5+ with Ti-O-P bonds; O 1s confirms increased oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The practical structure and elemental chemical state of Ru/P-TiO2 were investigated by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS); the XPS survey spectrum of Ru/P-TiO2 indicated the presence of Ru, P, O, and Ti (Figure S10)... In the high-resolution Ru 3d5/2 XPS spectra... Ru0 exhibited an additional negative shift of 0.06 eV when P was doped... the P 2p spectrum of Ru/P-TiO2 exhibited two peaks (at 133.2 and 134.3 eV), indicating the existence of P in the pentavalent state only... The increase in oxygen vacancies of Ru/P-TiO2 was also confirmed by the O 1s XPS (Figure S12)

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR confirms increase in oxygen vacancies of Ru/P-TiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The increase in oxygen vacancies of Ru/P-TiO2 was also confirmed by the O 1s XPS (Figure S12) and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) (Figure S13) spectra of Ru/P-TiO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows lower white-line absorption in Ru/P-TiO2 confirming enhanced backdonation of electrons from P-TiO2 to Ru d-bands; similar to metallic Ru indicating bulk-like antioxidation ability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2d shows the Ru K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of Ru/P-TiO2, Ru/TiO2, and the references. The lower white-line absorption of Ru/P-TiO2 relative to the d-p hybridized orbitals... confirmed an enhanced backdonation of electrons from P-TiO2 into the d bands of Ru...

properties.description: Complex with purple Ru center, cyan/blue ligands, red orbital overlay

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge EXAFS shows Ru-O-Ti at 1.65 Å and Ru-Ru at 2.31 Å in Ru/TiO2; positive shifts to 1.78 Å and 2.35 Å in Ru/P-TiO2; average coordination number of Ru decreases from 8.10 to 4.88 indicating increased vacancy defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectrum of Ru/TiO2 (Figure 2e) exhibited two main peaks at 1.65 and 2.31 Å corresponding to Ru-O-Ti and Ru-Ru interactions... Thus, the average coordination number of Ru changed from 8.10 (Ru-M and Ru-O) in Ru/TiO2 to 4.88 in Ru/P-TiO2...

nodes.evidence_snippet: The A2 feature of Ru/P-TiO2 exhibited a significant low-energy shift with higher intensity than that of Ru/TiO2, indicating a low coordination number of Ti... indicating mixed-phase TiO2 in Ru/P-TiO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ti K-edge EXAFS shows decreased Ti-O bond length in rutile phase and lower coordination number in Ru/P-TiO2 confirming partial substitution of Ti4+ by P5+ and increased oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2h, the introduction of Ru into TiO2 induced the formation of the rutile phase... Furthermore, the Ru/P-TiO2 catalyst exhibited a lower Ti-O coordination number compared to Ru/TiO2...

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Ru/P-TiO2 has smallest charge-transfer resistance among all catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru/P-TiO2 exhibited the smallest charge-transfer resistance among all the catalysts, according to the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) analysis...

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates (5-120 mV/s) used to calculate double-layer capacitance Cdl; Ru/P-TiO2 shows 1.27 times increase in surface area compared to Ru/TiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double-layer capacitance (Cdl) (Figure 3g) was evaluated from CV curves recorded with scan rates in the range of 5-120 mVs-1 (Figure S22), to estimate the effective electrochemical active surface area (ECSA).

nodes.characterization_summary: Wavelet transform of EXAFS shows Ru/P-TiO2 has coordination environment resembling bulk Ru metal with intensity maximum at 8.8 Å⁻¹ indicating strong metallic coordination and electron-rich Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The wavelet transforms (WT) of EXAFS were used to investigate the coordination features of Ru/P-TiO2 (Figure 2i)... the Ru/P-TiO2 exhibited a coordination environment resembling that of bulk Ru metal, with an intensity maximum at 8.8 Å⁻¹, indicating strong metallic coordination.
